archetype.name: Play-In Team (shot-making, turnover-prone)
archetype.definition: A team with a positive net rating and a defense that holds up, sitting in the league's middle because it gives away possessions and loses the glass, with no margin to make that up against the West's best.

report.headline: Elite shooting, league-worst turnovers: a 1-2 start better than it looks
report.take:
Three games in, the Clippers are a split personality. When they get a shot up, few teams are better: their eFG % of 58.3 ranks 3rd and their 3P % of 40.9 ranks 5th. Yet the offense rates only 16th, at 110.6 points per 100 possessions, because they turn it over more than anyone. Their TOV % of 20.2 ranks 30th, far above the league's 14.3. Add rebounding that ranks 25th in RPG and 20th in ORB %, and an efficient offense ends up average. The defense has carried them so far, 8th in DRtg at 107.3, helped by forcing turnovers (Opp TOV % 16.0, 7th) more than by stopping shots.

The record undersells the play. A +3.3 Net Rtg is 11th in the league. The margin implies two wins, not one, and W vs Pt Diff sits at -1. The two losses came on the road against the Lakers and Oklahoma City by single digits, and the win was a 25-point rout of Sacramento. That is a team being beaten by good opponents, not one being outplayed across the board.

The roster split is just as stark. Kris Dunn (BPM 7.6, TS % 73.4, 5th among point guards) and Brook Lopez (BPM 7.2, TS % 76.3, 7th among centers) have been excellent. Darius Garland is using 31.4% of possessions with a BPM of -4 and an On-Off of -46. Rui Hachimura's TS % of 36.9 and BPM of -10.7 are the main reason the frontcourt grades D+ despite Lopez. Three games of on-off data are mostly noise, but a ball-dominant guard turning a shooting team into a turnover team fits the numbers better than it should.

History says some of this corrects itself, in both directions. No recent Clippers team turned it over at even 14%; last season it was 13.2, so the turnover rate should fall sharply and the offense should climb. The 40.9% from three is also above anything they've posted in five seasons, and it will come down too. The real question is whether this defense is the 2024-25 version (3rd in defensive rank) or last year's 18th. Opponents taking 40.7% of their shots at the rim, the most in the league, points to the latter.

strengths.title: Shot-making near the top of the league
strengths.body: Their eFG % and TS % both rank 3rd, with 3P % 5th and a 3PA Rate above league average. Lopez, Dunn and Derrick Jones Jr. are all scoring above 70% TS %, so the efficiency is spread across the lineup. Expect some cooling, since the three-point rate is well above their five-year norms, but the shot profile is built to stay above average.

strengths.title: A defense that takes the ball
strengths.body: They rank 8th in DRtg, well below the league average in points allowed per 100, mostly by forcing turnovers (7th) and holding opponents' wings and power forwards to almost nothing. Whether it lasts is open: they ranked 18th in defense last season, and the shots they allow are not being contested especially well.

strengths.title: Dunn and Lopez driving the good minutes
strengths.body: Dunn ranks 5th of 78 point guards on low usage with a 73.4 TS %. Lopez ranks 7th of 73 centers with a positive On-Off. They are the two most efficient regulars and the clearest case for playing more two-way minutes through them.

concerns.title: Giving the ball away constantly
concerns.body: A TOV % of 20.2 is last in the league and far above anything in their recent history (13.2 last season). It is the single biggest reason elite shooting produces only a 16th-ranked offense. It should regress toward normal, but with Garland using 31.4% of possessions at a negative BPM, the cause looks structural as well as random.

concerns.title: Soft at the rim and on the glass
concerns.body: Opponents take 40.7% of their shots at the rim, the most in the league and well above their own recent seasons, and finish them at a 21st-ranked rate. The Clippers also rank 25th in RPG and 20th in ORB %. The frontcourt's D+ grade reflects this, with Hachimura's 36.9 TS % and -10.7 BPM dragging down what Lopez provides.

concerns.title: Shooting guards are torching them
concerns.body: Opposing shooting guards account for 45.6% of the points scored against the Clippers, against a league share of 25%. They are also posting well above their usual production. Three games is a tiny sample, but it is the one leak in an otherwise stingy perimeter defense.

trend.note: Three games: a blowout win at home and two single-digit road losses to strong teams. The margin implies two wins, so the record trails the play slightly, but the sample is too small to call a direction.

weekAhead.headline: Two unbeaten teams and Toronto's turnover machine: the season's first real test
weekAhead.body:
The week opens with a rematch against the 3-0 Lakers, whose offense ranks 1st in ORtg at 126.5 but whose defense ranks only 18th and whose rebounding is the league's worst by RPG. That is a rare matchup where the Clippers' glass problem won't be punished, and the Lakers have been generous to point guards. Then comes the hardest stop: at Minnesota, the site's No. 1 team. The Timberwolves rank 1st in DRtg, DRB % and REB % and 2nd in ORB %, which attacks exactly what the Clippers do worst.

The back end is consecutive days. First is Golden State on the road, 0-3 with the 29th-ranked DRtg and the worst Opp eFG % and Opp Rim FG %, the best chance at an efficient night. The next day Toronto visits with the 3rd-ranked defense and the league's best Opp TOV %, a direct test of the Clippers' biggest flaw. Toronto's own offense is among the worst-shooting in the league, though. A 2-2 week would be a solid result; anything better likely requires the turnover rate to start falling.

keyMatchups.title: Minnesota's glass vs. the Clippers' boards
keyMatchups.body: Minnesota leads the league in REB % and RPG and sits 2nd in ORB %, while the Clippers rank 25th in RPG. Second chances could decide that game before shooting does. Minnesota also holds shooting guards to very little, limiting a usual secondary option.

keyMatchups.title: Toronto's hands vs. LAC's turnovers
keyMatchups.body: Toronto forces turnovers at the league's highest rate, and the Clippers commit them at the highest. Toronto's offense ranks 29th in eFG %, so if the Clippers simply hold onto the ball, their shooting edge should win the game.

keyMatchups.title: Lakers' leaky point-guard defense
keyMatchups.body: The Lakers have allowed 36.33 points a game to point guards, among the most in the league, and rank 28th in DRB %. Dunn and Garland get a favorable matchup, and the Clippers' weak offensive rebounding may finally find some room.

weekAhead.watch: Whether the TOV % starts falling toward last season's level, especially against Toronto on the second of the back-to-back nights.

restOfSeason.body:
The underlying shape points to a .500-plus team in the 42 to 50-win band the franchise has lived in for five seasons. The turnover rate is an outlier that should normalize and lift the offense. The shooting will also cool from 40.9% on threes, so the two roughly offset, and the net result is a mid-pack offense. The defense decides how high they finish. Forcing turnovers is a repeatable skill, but allowing the most rim attempts in the league usually catches up with a team, and last season's 18th-ranked defense is a fair warning.

I'd project 40 to 47 wins, a Net Rtg between roughly 0 and +3.5, and a TOV % settling in the 14 to 16 range. That's a play-in-level team that could climb if the Dunn-Lopez minutes keep winning and Hachimura's shooting recovers.
swingFactors: Rim protection and rebounding beyond Lopez

confidence.note: Three games; shooting and turnover rates far from team history.
